name: Caesars Entertainment
description: Caesars owns, leases or manages 52 casino resorts in 18 US states (the Las Vegas Strip resorts, Harrah's, Horseshoe, Eldorado, Isle and Tropicana regional casinos) and runs the Caesars Sportsbook, Caesars Palace Online Casino, Horseshoe Online Casino and Caesars Racebook apps. Gambling is the core: casino operations (slots, tables, retail and online betting) were about 58% of 2025 revenue, with hotel rooms about 17% and food and beverage about 15%. Many of the real estate assets are leased from the landlords GLPI and VICI, and the company carries heavy debt (net interest expense $2.3 billion in 2025 against $3.6 billion of Adjusted EBITDA), so it reported a net loss of $502 million for 2025. On May 27, 2026 it agreed to be bought by Fertitta Gaming Holdco for $31.00 a share in cash; stockholders approved on September 22, 2026 and regulatory approvals are pending.

businessLines.name: Las Vegas
businessLines.how: Customers gamble at the casinos (slots, tables, sports betting) and Caesars keeps the win after paying gaming tax, while hotel rooms, food and beverage, shows and the convention center add non-gaming revenue from the same visitors; revenue moves with Las Vegas visitor counts and how much they spend.
businessLines.description: Caesars Palace, The Cromwell, Flamingo, Harrah's Las Vegas, Horseshoe Las Vegas, The LINQ, Paris Las Vegas, Planet Hollywood (FY2025 list), plus the Caesars Forum conference center, the High Roller wheel and Fly LINQ zipline. The Vanderpump Hotel is added to the list in the Q2 2026 10-Q.

operatingProfit.note: Segment Adjusted EBITDA (the only segment profit measure reported); FY2024 $1,907M; FY2023 $2,016M

businessLines.name: Regional
businessLines.how: Local and drive-in customers gamble at slots and tables and Caesars keeps the win after gaming taxes (about $1.26 billion of gaming tax in 2025, roughly a fifth of segment revenue), with smaller hotel, food and beverage and entertainment revenue; competition from tribal casinos and new openings in nearby markets is the main pressure.
businessLines.description: Casino resorts outside Las Vegas, for example Harrah's, Horseshoe, Isle, Eldorado, Tropicana, Caesars New Orleans, Caesars Virginia and Caesars Atlantic City; Caesars Windsor (Ontario) moved into this segment in 2026.

revenue.note: Casino $4,193M; food and beverage $616M; hotel $632M; other $315M. FY2024 $5,539M; FY2023 $5,778M

businessLines.revenueNote: Casino $4,193M; food and beverage $616M; hotel $632M; other $315M. FY2024 $5,539M; FY2023 $5,778M

businessLines.name: Caesars Digital
businessLines.how: Bettors stake money online and Caesars keeps the hold (the share of handle it does not pay out) on sports bets and online casino games, minus state gaming taxes, marketing and platform costs; revenue grows by launching in newly legalized states and winning customers.
businessLines.description: Caesars Sportsbook, Caesars Racebook, Caesars Palace Online Casino and Horseshoe Online Casino apps on the in-house Liberty platform; online sports betting in 27 jurisdictions and iGaming in five at 2025 year end.

businessLines.name: Managed and Branded
businessLines.how: Fees: Caesars is paid to run casinos owned by others (partly reimbursement of payroll for managed properties) and a fee to let a property use the Caesars name and marks.
businessLines.description: Casinos Caesars manages for others (for example Harrah's Cherokee, Harrah's Ak-Chin and Harrah's Resort Southern California) and properties licensed to use the Caesars brands (for example Caesars Southern Indiana and Harrah's Northern California).
